batch: Classify seven works from university and publisher evidence
policy: These are work-scope judgments only. They do not certify complete object extraction, endorse readings, resolve identities or authenticity, or change text and media rights.

entries.basis: HSE University's abstract says the paper is the first publication of all eleven State Hermitage incantation bowls, based on collations of the originals.
Wayne State University Press describes a comprehensive study of early Jewish magic, its sources, methods and scholarship, treating bowls within a wider evidentiary synthesis.
The complete article hosted by the Trafficking Culture research project examines the legal and ethical problems of collecting and studying unprovenanced, likely looted incantation bowls.
The journal abstract describes a focused response to arguments over the edition and terminology for BM 135563, not a new edition or bounded corpus.
The publisher preview calls the chapter a preliminary survey of Mandaic-script magic texts in the Moussaieff Collection and distinguishes it from editions published or being prepared elsewhere.
The journal places this four-page scholarly discussion in its Reviews section; it reviews Aramaic Bowl Spells volume one and is not the corpus edition itself.

Brill places the two-page contribution in Recensioni, and the publisher-hosted text reviews Moriggi's corpus coverage, editorial method and linguistic contribution rather than presenting another object edition.
